title: La Touche and Le Mercier de La Rivière (Martinique) to the Navy minister, 12 June 1761 (ANOM COL C8 A 64 f° 1)

documents.shelfmark: Archives nationales d'outre-mer, COL C8 A 64 f° 1 (duplicata)

plaintext.source: Margin note says it was deciphered on arrival ('déchiffrée et remise à M. Accaron par M. Villain'), but no decipherment is filed with it.

transcription.notes: Clear letter with long runs of comma-separated 2-3 digit groups on images 2-5; four caret insertions; 514/614 and 553/653 the main doubtful readings.

documents.shelfmark: Archives nationales d'outre-mer, COL C8 A 63 f° 208 (no. 178, primata)

plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherment written above every code line.

transcription.notes: Sibling used as key source; 19 clear|code pairs.

system.summary: Numerical nomenclator of about 700 groups (values 11-696), probably a two-part syllabic code like the printed Navy form used for Martinique in 1765; clear words embedded in the cipher runs.
system.sibling_key: C8 A 63 f° 208 (no. 178, 21 Aug 1761), same code with interlinear decipherment

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherment by Villain for Accaron (margin note); not located. Nothing in print or online.

conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue 542 task; selected the target.

solution.what: Opened the five ANOM images via the FranceArchives manifest in the browser (direct curl gets 403).
Transcribed the clear text and all code runs: 818 groups, 217 distinct, values 11-696; margin note shows the letter was deciphered at the time by Villain.
'423, D.. 614. Choiseul' read as 'M. le Duc de Choiseul': 614 = de (hypothesis).
Web search on shelfmark, correspondents and date: no published decipherment.
Tested the 1765 Martinique key (ANOM C8 A 67 f° 178, for d'Ennery): 614 = voisins, 674 = trou, de = 428, values up to ~800; does not fit.
Listed the seven 1761 joint letters (C8 A 63-64); none described as ciphered; C8 A 64 f° 4 viewed, clear.
Found Archives nationales MAR/G/178, Navy keys for colonial dispatches 1741-1776 (1758, 1766, 1771, printed treatise 1776); not digitised.
Completed the 1765 deciphering table, all 800 entries (key1765_ennery.tsv), as the unit vocabulary.

Annealing group -> 1765-form unit, fr-modern order-5 LM + unit prior, on held-out d'Affry 1757 French enciphered in the letter's shape (818 tokens, 218 types), 1M iterations, 2 seeds: 7.7% / 8.9% correct; found key outscores truth.

Added a word-segmentation score (x3): 7.3% / 4.8% correct; found still outscores truth (-21088 vs -21356, -21465 vs -22780). Objective cannot separate the true text at this length and vocabulary size.
Same solver on the letter: word salad, 614 = es against the 614 = de crib. Not meaningful given the failed control.
Inventory search found C8 A 63 f° 208 (La Rivière no. 178, 21 Aug 1761), same code with interlinear decipherment; transcribed 19 clear|code pairs.
Aligned the sibling pairs: ~110 values (Saint Eustache = 371 201 674 361 313 x3; 614 = de; 423 = le; 674 = s). Applied to the target: 67.0% of tokens valued.

Context in the target: vo, so/tion, i/an, é/ant, di/ge, mo/g/mon, cu, ca, ar, cha and others from repeated phrases (nous avons/devons, consommation, soixante, étant venus, Monseigneur, moitié, spéculation, arriver, de change). Coverage 75.2%.
COL B 113/114 (outgoing registers 1761-62) located; not digitised.

Three rounds of context valuation with kwic.py (541 = u, d/ra, si, po, lu/autre, cent/douze, no, ex, go, lo, ou, va, denrée, lettre ...). Valued 89.1% of tokens; measure_sense.py (dictionary segmentation of each decoded run) gives 81.5% read as sense.

Retry round: odd spots re-checked on the images (two encipherer slips), every open group retried with kwic.py, 22 values added (pos, soien, puis, ir, nos, com, an, fond, parei, qui, y + C-grade). 93.0% valued, 86.7% read as sense (measured).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from the contemporary interlinear decipherment of sibling letter C8 A 63 f° 208 (same file series, same correspondents, 1761), extended from context in the target. 93.0% of tokens valued, 86.7% read as sense (measure_sense.py); about 46 groups, mostly occurring once, still open.
outcome.notes: In progress toward the read bar. Leads: more context work; image sweep of C8 A 63-64; COL B 113/114 and MAR/G/178 offline.

gaps.item: about 46 code groups (57 tokens), single-occurrence word codes
gaps.detail: thin context; still to be tried

gaps.item: C-grade values resting on one context

gaps.detail: groups clear on the image but wrong as written; read by sense, marked [?]
